value_chain.value_chain_position: Scaleway is a French cloud computing and AI infrastructure provider, operating as a majority-owned subsidiary of the Iliad Group (Europe's 5th-largest telecom, EUR 10B group revenue in 2024). It sits between GPU hardware suppliers (NVIDIA) upstream and AI model creators, enterprises, and startups downstream. Scaleway offers IaaS and PaaS services including GPU compute, managed Kubernetes, object storage, and AI-specific tooling. Its strategic differentiator is providing European sovereign AI compute -- it is one of the largest commercially available AI computing platforms in Europe with nearly 5,000 top-tier GPUs. Scaleway hosts Mistral AI's training workloads (the Mixtral model was trained on Scaleway's Nabuchodonosor supercomputer) and is one of NVIDIA's selected European partners for DGX Cloud Lepton, the global federated GPU marketplace. The Iliad Group has committed EUR 3B to AI infrastructure across Scaleway, OpCore (its spun-off data center subsidiary), and Kyutai (its AI research lab). Scaleway's data centers are physically owned by OpCore (valued at EUR 860M, with InfraVia acquiring a 50% stake in 2025), while Scaleway operates the cloud software and services layer on top.

key_products: GPU Cloud & AI Supercomputers: NVIDIA H100, H200, L40S, and Blackwell Ultra GPU instances for AI training and inference, accessible on-demand or via reserved capacity. Includes Nabuchodonosor ('Nabu'), an NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with 1,016 H100 GPUs and InfiniBand networking, hosted at the Iliad Group's DC5 data center near Paris. Offers AI Notebooks, AI Training pipelines, and AI Deploy (serverless inference) for the full ML lifecycle. SLURM and Kubernetes orchestration for large-scale distributed training. Minute-by-minute billing with competitive H100 pricing among European providers. Selected by NVIDIA for DGX Cloud Lepton, providing European sovereign compute to the global NVIDIA developer ecosystem.

Public Cloud IaaS/PaaS: Full-stack cloud platform including virtual instances (x86 and ARM), bare metal servers, managed Kubernetes (Kosmos multi-cloud control plane), object storage (S3-compatible), block storage, managed databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis), serverless functions and containers, load balancers, VPC networking, and IoT Hub. Data centers in Paris (DC2-DC5), Amsterdam, and Warsaw, with European expansion planned. Built on open standards (OpenStack-compatible APIs, CNCF Kubernetes) for portability and minimal vendor lock-in.

AI Model Marketplace & Managed AI Services: Access to Mistral AI's full model suite and H Company's Holo 2 through Scaleway's platform. Partnership with Mistral AI and NVIDIA for the DGX Cloud Lepton marketplace, enabling startups and developers to access foundation models alongside compute infrastructure. Managed inference endpoints with integrated model serving. Positions Scaleway as both an infrastructure and AI platform layer for European customers.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Scaleway does not report standalone revenue; its financials are consolidated within the Iliad Group (Euronext Paris: ILD). Iliad Group total revenue: EUR 10.0B in 2024 (+8.5% YoY), with EBITDAaL of EUR 3.85B (+11.8%). Scaleway's cloud revenue grew 37% in 2024, with more than 20% of Scaleway revenue now coming from AI workloads. Third-party estimates place Scaleway's annual revenue in the range of EUR 150-250M, though this is not officially confirmed. The Iliad Group has committed EUR 3B specifically to AI infrastructure investment across Scaleway, OpCore, and Kyutai. OpCore (the spun-off data center subsidiary) was valued at EUR 860M enterprise value when InfraVia acquired a 50% stake in 2025. [uncertain]
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: Not publicly reported as a standalone figure. Scaleway's cloud services are subscription and usage-based, implying predominantly recurring revenue. One third-party source estimated Scaleway at $17.5M revenue with 300K customers in 2021, but the company has grown significantly since, with 37% cloud revenue growth in 2024 and major GPU infrastructure expansion. Current ARR is not disclosed separately from Iliad Group financials. [uncertain]
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Not applicable in the traditional startup sense. Scaleway is a subsidiary of the publicly traded Iliad Group (Euronext Paris: ILD, market cap ~EUR 12B). Founded by Xavier Niel in 1999, the company is funded through Iliad Group's operating cash flow and capital allocation. Iliad has committed EUR 3B to AI infrastructure (Feb 2025), and OpCore (the data center arm spun off from Scaleway) received investment from InfraVia (50% stake at EUR 860M enterprise value). OpCore plans EUR 2.5B investment in hyperscale data center expansion. No independent venture rounds for Scaleway itself.
business.business_model: Usage-based and subscription cloud computing, mirroring the standard IaaS/PaaS model. Revenue streams: (1) GPU compute rental (H100, H200, Blackwell instances -- per-minute billing); (2) Public cloud IaaS (virtual instances, bare metal, storage -- hourly/monthly billing); (3) PaaS managed services (Kubernetes, databases, serverless); (4) AI platform services (notebooks, training, inference endpoints); (5) Web hosting (legacy business from Online.net era). Competitive pricing relative to hyperscalers, with transparent pricing and a focus on European customers requiring data sovereignty. Revenue is predominantly recurring through cloud subscriptions.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Not applicable -- Scaleway is a subsidiary of the profitable Iliad Group. Iliad reported EUR 3.85B EBITDAaL in 2024 (+11.8% YoY) and EUR 503M operating free cash flow in Q1 2025 (+9.3%). The group self-funds Scaleway's growth and GPU infrastructure expansion through operating cash flow. No standalone burn rate concerns.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Hybrid (open-source-friendly infrastructure). Scaleway builds on open-source technologies: OpenStack-compatible APIs, CNCF-certified Kubernetes, Kosmos multi-cloud Kubernetes control plane. Does not develop proprietary foundation models. Promotes interoperability, portability, and minimal vendor lock-in as core value propositions. Open APIs and standard protocols throughout. Customers can deploy any open-source or proprietary AI model on Scaleway infrastructure. Was a founding member of GAIA-X but departed the project in 2021, citing a preference for delivering sovereignty values through product rather than consortium compliance.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: Scaleway is strategically important for European AI startups and a key case study for the course for several reasons: (1) Sovereign AI infrastructure: For startups deploying AI in regulated European sectors (health, finance, public sector), Scaleway provides French/EU-hosted GPU compute that avoids US CLOUD Act exposure -- this is increasingly important as the EU AI Act takes effect (Aug 2025 onward) and French/European public procurement favors sovereign cloud; (2) GPU accessibility: Nearly 5,000 top-tier GPUs (H100, H200, Blackwell Ultra) available commercially, with minute-by-minute billing and no long-term commitment required -- significantly more accessible than trying to secure GPU allocations from AWS/Azure/GCP, where AI startups often face waitlists; (3) Mistral AI case study: Scaleway's Nabuchodonosor supercomputer was used to train Mistral's Mixtral model, demonstrating that world-class AI models can be trained on European infrastructure -- this is a powerful narrative for European tech sovereignty; (4) Competitive pricing: Scaleway offers some of the lowest H100 hourly rates among major cloud GPU providers, extending runway for cash-constrained startups; (5) Startup Program: Up to EUR 36,000 in cloud credits over 24 months through partner accelerators, plus a dedicated NVIDIA Inception program for GPU-intensive startups; (6) NVIDIA DGX Cloud Lepton integration: Scaleway's inclusion in NVIDIA's global GPU marketplace means startups can access Scaleway's European compute alongside the broader NVIDIA ecosystem; (7) No vendor lock-in: Built on Kubernetes and open standards, making it straightforward to migrate workloads if needed; (8) Part of a larger ecosystem: The Iliad Group's EUR 3B AI commitment and backing from Xavier Niel (France's most prominent tech investor) signals long-term stability and investment continuity.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Highly accessible for startups. Scaleway Startup Program offers up to EUR 1,000 initial cloud credits, scaling to EUR 9,000 for go-to-market stage startups, and up to EUR 36,000 over 24 months through accelerator and VC partnerships. Dedicated NVIDIA Inception startup program for GPU-intensive workloads. Pay-as-you-go pricing with minute-by-minute billing on GPU instances, no minimum commitment. GPU instances (H100, H200, L40S, Blackwell Ultra) available on-demand. Managed Kubernetes included at no extra charge (pay only for underlying compute). Extensive documentation in English and French. API-first approach with standard interfaces. Pricing significantly below hyperscaler equivalents for comparable GPU resources.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None. Scaleway is infrastructure-layer and does not depend on any specific foundation model. Hosts and enables deployment of any model. Provides access to Mistral AI's full model suite and H Company's Holo 2 through its platform, but these are partnership integrations, not dependencies. Customers can deploy Mistral, Llama, or any other model on Scaleway GPU instances.

ecosystem.key_partnerships: NVIDIA: strategic partnership for GPU supply (H100, H200, Blackwell Ultra), selected as one of the first European providers for DGX Cloud Lepton sovereign compute marketplace, NVIDIA Spectrum-X networking technology deployed. Mistral AI: flagship AI customer -- Mixtral trained on Nabuchodonosor supercomputer, full Mistral model suite available through Scaleway platform, joint participation in DGX Cloud Lepton marketplace. Iliad Group: parent company (Euronext: ILD), providing EUR 3B AI investment commitment and access to OpCore data center infrastructure (13 data centers). InfraVia: acquired 50% of OpCore at EUR 860M enterprise value to fund EUR 2.5B hyperscale expansion. H Company: Holo 2 model accessible through Scaleway platform. Play (Poland): strategic partnership bringing European cloud and AI solutions to Polish businesses. France Televisions: public broadcaster using Scaleway's cloud platform. ANSSI: pursuing SecNumCloud 3.2 qualification (target: end 2025). Kyutai: Iliad-funded AI research lab leveraging Scaleway infrastructure.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: European sovereignty positioning: Scaleway is pursuing ANSSI SecNumCloud 3.2 qualification (target end 2025), which will provide the highest French/EU data sovereignty guarantee -- a structural advantage that US hyperscalers cannot replicate due to the CLOUD Act. This positions Scaleway for European public sector and regulated industry procurement where sovereignty is required by law. Largest European commercial AI compute: With nearly 5,000 top-tier GPUs and NVIDIA's Nabuchodonosor DGX SuperPOD, Scaleway operates one of the largest commercially available AI computing capacities in Europe. Xavier Niel / Iliad backing: Backed by France's most prominent tech billionaire and a EUR 10B telecom group with EUR 3B committed specifically to AI -- providing financial stability and long-term investment horizon that independent startups cannot match. NVIDIA preferred European partner: Selection for DGX Cloud Lepton and early access to Blackwell Ultra creates a privileged position in the NVIDIA ecosystem. Vertical integration through OpCore: Data center ownership (13 facilities) provides cost structure control and capacity guarantees. Open standards approach: Kubernetes and OpenStack-based platform reduces vendor lock-in anxiety for customers, differentiating from proprietary hyperscaler services.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: Exempt from GPAI provider obligations under EU AI Act (does not develop foundation models). Positioned as a beneficiary and compliance enabler: Scaleway's infrastructure helps customers meet EU AI Act hosting and data residency requirements for high-risk AI systems. Actively pursuing ANSSI SecNumCloud 3.2 qualification (passed J0 milestone, targeting end 2025), which provides the highest level of French/EU cloud security certification. GDPR compliant by design -- all data centers in EU (France, Netherlands, Poland), no exposure to US CLOUD Act. Former GAIA-X founding member (departed 2021, citing preference for delivering sovereignty through product). Parent company Iliad is publicly traded (Euronext Paris: ILD) with associated SEC-equivalent French AMF reporting obligations.
